paragraphs: It is Saturday evening, and Mom is out. Mom's telephone rings in the living room. Lily looks at the screen. "It is Aunt Sue!" she says. Aunt Sue calls from Chiang Mai on a phone app. Lily sits on the sofa, and Pip sits next to her. "Hello, Lily! How old are you now?" asks Aunt Sue. "I am nine," says Lily. "Who is at home?" asks Aunt Sue. "My brother Tom is here, and Dad is at work," says Lily. "What is Tom like now?" asks Aunt Sue. "He is very tall and very loud!" says Lily.

Aunt Sue is a nurse at a hospital in Chiang Mai. She works every day, but she always calls Lily's family. "How often do you travel to see us?" asks Lily. "Not often," says Aunt Sue. "Some nights I am awake, and the sick children are asleep." "Is someone with you?" asks Aunt Sue. "Yes, Pip is here," says Lily. She holds the phone up to the puppy. "Woof!" says Pip. "Is he awake?" asks Aunt Sue. "Yes, he is not asleep at all!" says Lily. They chat about Pip and his red ball.

Aunt Sue says her new number slowly. "Zero, eight, one, four, five, five, two, two, nine, six." "Pardon?" says Lily. "The line is bad," says Aunt Sue. She says the number again, and Lily says "Pardon?" again. "Shall I write it down?" asks Lily. Tom comes in and laughs at the phone. Lily writes the number on a note and puts it on the fridge. Mom comes home. "Really?" says Mom. "Aunt Sue is on the phone?" Lily gives the phone to Mom. "How about a kiss for Pip?" says Aunt Sue. Lily gives Pip a big kiss, and he says, "Woof!"
text.summary: Aunt Sue calls from Chiang Mai on a Saturday evening. Lily answers the phone, and they talk about Tom, Pip, and Aunt Sue's new number.
